title: Harrell et al. v. Covenant Presbytery
disposition_detail: Appeal sustained as to Specifications 1–3 (indictment specificity; refusal of particulars; guilty verdicts), and not sustained as to Specifications 4–8 (disqualification of Session members/witnesses, TE Wreyford, TE Norton; venue; refusal to refer to Presbytery). The SJC reversed the lower courts' judgments and the guilty verdicts; no remand or further proceedings are specified.
first_summary: The SJC sustained an appeal by seven members of a mission church convicted by their temporary Session for opposing the organizing minister's expected election as pastor. It reversed the guilty verdicts and the Presbytery's affirmance, holding the indictments lacked BCO 32-5 specificity, the Session had no authority over pastoral selection, and no Fifth or Ninth Commandment offense was proved. The SJC rejected challenges to witness-judges, venue, and refusal to refer the trial.
summary: The SJC sustained an appeal by seven members of a 38-member mission church who were convicted by their temporary Session of opposing the organizing minister's expected election as pastor. Reversing the Presbytery's affirmance and the guilty verdicts underlying indefinite suspensions, the SJC held the indictments fatally lacked BCO 32-5 specificity; Presbytery used the wrong standard of review; the Session had no authority to control pastoral selection; and no Fifth or Ninth Commandment offense was proved. Challenges to witness-judges, venue, and refusal to refer were rejected.

evidence_notes.outcomes_and_reasons: SJC sustained Specifications 1–3 and did not sustain 4–8; guilty verdicts reversed. Reasons: BCO 32-5 indictment specificity, BCO 39/43 rather than BCO 40-5 standard of review, no Fifth or Ninth Commandment violations, and no Sessional authority over pastoral selection, lines 179–190, 194–235, 297–391, 393–425.
